fact: The BCEAO's PI-SPI instant payment platform counts 175 authorised participants across the eight WAEMU countries, with Senegal holding the most at 43, and Wave was authorised to open its services in Senegal on the list updated 30 September 2026.
BCEAO counted 31 licensed payment institutions in the UMOA at end of February 2026, 11 of them in Senegal, under its 23 January 2024 instruction on payment services.
BCEAO launched PI-SPI, the regional interoperable instant payment platform, on 30 September 2025, running 24/7; 80 participants were connected at 24 June 2026.
Senegal is within the UMOA regional instant payment platform PI-SPI launched by BCEAO on 30 September 2025, with 80 participants connected at 24 June 2026.
The BCEAO list, updated 26 September 2025, names 13 Senegal participants authorised to open PI-SPI services to the public at the 30 September 2025 launch.
Financial Afrik says BCEAO operates the PI-SPI instant-payment system, with 19 Senegal institutions authorised on its list, the most in the Union.
Financial Afrik says 19 Senegal institutions are authorised by BCEAO to offer PI-SPI, the WAEMU regional real-time payment system.
BCEAO lists 11 authorised electronic money initiatives in Senegal at 30 September 2024: three licensed e-money issuers and eight banks issuing through partners.

BCEAO's national director says that under instruction 01-01-2024 fintechs need BCEAO approval; nine are approved in the UEMOA area, two (Pay Dunya and Mikati) in Senegal, and non-compliant operators have been suspended since 2 May 2025.
The Africa Report says Wave holds an e-money issuer licence granted by the BCEAO in Senegal.
Launch Base Africa reports the BCEAO runs PI-SPI, the shared instant payment platform through which interoperable e-money transfers have had to route since 2 November 2026, covering Senegal.
Le Soleil reports the BCEAO's PI-SPI instant interoperable payment platform, launched 30 September 2025, carries bank-wallet transfers in Senegal and is mandatory from 2 November 2026.
Le Soleil reports PI-SPI, the BCEAO's platform, is the mandatory route for interoperable e-money transactions across the eight UEMOA states including Senegal.

BiFinances says the BCEAO's PI-SPI platform, launched 30 September 2025, runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and that on 2 April 2026 the BCEAO counted 80 connected participants including nine e-money institutions.
BiFinances reports Wave announced on 6 November 2026 that its customers in Senegal can use the BCEAO's regional PI-SPI platform from its app; this is a regional system, not PAPSS.
